title: Teleological and Ontological Arguments
welcome_lead: Move from Paley's watch on the heath to Anselm's Proslogion in the cloister, weighing arguments from design and from concept alone.
meta_desc: A-Level Religious Studies adventure on teleological and ontological arguments: Paley, Hume, Anselm, Gaunilo, Descartes, and Plantinga.
final_note: You have seen the two great a posteriori and a priori arguments for God across centuries of debate.

concepts.term: Aliquid Quo Nihil Maius Cogitari Possit
concepts.def: Anselm's Latin formula: 'that than which nothing greater can be conceived'.
Plantinga's version using possible-worlds semantics to argue that maximal greatness in some world entails it in every world.

walkthroughs.body_html: In Natural Theology (1802), William Paley imagines finding a watch on a heath. Its intricate parts working together for a purpose imply a designer. So too, the eye, the wing of a bird, and the order of nature imply a divine artificer. Hume's Dialogues (1779) had pre-empted the argument: the universe is not a machine but more like a vegetable; we cannot infer one designer rather than many.

Anselm (c.1078) defines God as id quo maius cogitari nequit. Even the fool of Psalm 14 understands the concept. But existence in reality is greater than existence in the understanding alone. So the greatest conceivable being must exist in reality. Gaunilo replied with the perfect island; Anselm retorted that only God's essence and existence are inseparable.

Descartes (Meditation V, 1641) treats existence as a perfection. Kant objected that existence is not a predicate. Alvin Plantinga's modal version (1974) argues: there is a possible world in which a maximally great being exists; maximal greatness includes necessary existence; therefore such a being exists in every possible world, including ours.

mcqs.q: What does the teleological (design) argument claim?
options: The design argument proves God created the world in seven days.
The ontological argument is the same as the cosmological argument.
Apparent purpose, order or complexity in the universe implies an intelligent designer — Paley's watchmaker analogy is the classic example.
The design argument proves evolution is false.

mcqs.q: What is distinctive about the ontological argument?
options: It tries to prove God's existence purely from the concept of God — a priori reasoning needing no empirical evidence about the world.
The design argument proves evolution is false.
The ontological argument uses scientific evidence to prove God exists.
The ontological argument is the same as the cosmological argument.
